title: Andrew Henderson aims to build the largest private collection of Cambodian paintings in the world
summary: Andrew Henderson , best known as the founder of Nomad Capitalist, is developing Vesper Collection with a clear ambition: to build the world’s largest private collection of Cambodian paintings. The project grows out of thirteen years of visiting Cambodia and an attachment that has become increasingly personal. Henderson has become a Cambodian citizen and is building relationships with artists whose work he wants to collect, live with and bring to a wider audience. “I believe in the future of Asia, and I see Cambodia as one of its most up-and-coming countries,” Henderson says. “There’s something about Phnom Penh that reminds me of the creative atmosphere of Paris in Hemingway’s time. I want to be part of that.”

title: Renaissance nun receives one-woman show in New York
summary: Plautilla Nelli, an imaginative Dominican nun and the first Florentine woman to achieve fame as a painter, is the subject of a monographic exhibition—the first devoted to her outside of her native city—at the Upper East Side gallery of Robert Simon Fine Art. Opening 19 October, "Suor Plautilla Nelli: La Prima" will feature fourteen paintings and one drawing by or directly connected with the workshop she established at the Convent of Santa Caterina in Cafaggio, located across the piazza from the Monastery of San Marco in Florence. Heralded by Giorgio Vasari in his Lives of the Artists as "the first" among contemporary women painters—giving the exhibition its title—Nelli has been the subject of recent scholarly attention and restoration initiatives in Italy, as well as a 2017 exhibition at the Uffizi. title: MFA, St. Petersburg bets a Monet on a Tampa Bay Rays World Series victory
summary: The Museum of Fine Arts, St. Petersburg is showing its support for the Tampa Bay Rays in a big-league way. It’s putting a Monet in play. As the Tampa Bay Rays and the Milwaukee Brewers face off in the World Series, the MFA and the Milwaukee Art Museum have agreed to a friendly wager. Each institution is backing its team with a beloved painting by Claude Monet. The museum on the losing side will send its painting on loan to the winning team’s hometown for a victory lap in the galleries. If the Rays bring home the championship, St. Petersburg will welcome Milwaukee’s Waterloo Bridge, Sunlight Effect. title: Art, devotion and dramatic light: Francisco de Zurbarán's influence takes center stage at Mexico's Museo de Guadalupe
summary: The dramatic interplay of light and shadow that defined some of the most memorable paintings of the Spanish Baroque comes to life at Mexico's Museo de Guadalupe, where a new exhibition explores the artistic legacy of Francisco de Zurbarán and his influence on religious painting in colonial Mexico. Titled Vestidas para el cielo. Ecos virreinales de Francisco de Zurbarán (Dressed for Heaven: Viceregal Echoes of Francisco de Zurbarán), the exhibition brings together nine 17th-century oil paintings that reveal how art, faith and fashion converged during the Baroque period. Organized by Mexico's Ministry of Culture through the National Institute of Anthropology and History (INAH), the exhibition remains on view through February 21, 2027. title: Edward Hopper House Museum presents Susan Chen's first museum solo exhibition
summary: This fall, the Edward Hopper House Museum & Study Center presents Susan Chen: Rooms by the Sea, marking the New York–based artist’s first museum solo exhibition. On view through February 21, 2027, the exhibition brings together a series of Chen’s richly hued, energetic plein air paintings of Cape Cod, Massachusetts, alongside works on paper and watercolors by Edward Hopper and by Josephine Nivison Hopper. Centered around Chen’s recent large-scale double portrait, Rooms by the Sea (2026)—a direct tribute to Edward Hopper’s iconic 1951 masterpiece of the same title at the Yale University Art Gallery depicting his Truro studio —the exhibition explores the Outer Cape of Massachusetts through her vibrant, contemporary lens. As a first-generation American artist, Susan Chen (b. 1992, Hong Kong SAR) weaves personal history, cross-cultural perspective, and deep ecological observation into the traditional lineage of American landscape painting. title: Tiffany masterworks lead Heritage's strongest Early 20th Century Design Auction to date
summary: A Tiffany Studios Pony Wisteria table lamp leads Heritage's Nov. 11 Early 20th Century Design Signature® Auction, a 230-lot offering distinguished by the most important property and highest pre-auction estimates in the category's history at Heritage. With outstanding Tiffany lamps and a luminous figural window, a particularly strong selection of René Lalique and an exceptional group of Loetz glass, the auction marks a new high point for a department whose growth has made Heritage a leading destination for collectors of art glass. "The growth of our Design department has brought us to an extraordinary moment," says Samantha Robinson, Heritage's Vice President of Design. "Collectors increasingly turn to Heritage both to acquire exceptional glass and to entrust us with their collections, and that confidence is reflected in the quality of this sale. title: James-Simon-Galerie hosts landmark Genghis Khan exhibition in Berlin
summary: The year 2027 marks the 800th anniversary of Genghis Khan's death. To commemorate this occasion, the Museum für Vor- und Frühgeschichte of the Staatliche Museen zu Berlin, in collaboration with its Mongolian partners, is presenting the large-scale special exhibition "Genghis Khan and the world of the Mongols" at the James-Simon-Galerie. It tells the story of the Mongol Empire through significant archaeological finds from Mongolia and Europe. Most of the Mongolian objects on display are being shown outside the country for the first time. The exhibition focuses on new findings from Mongolian-German research and offers a nuanced perspective on an empire that had a lasting political, economic, and cultural impact on Eurasia. The special exhibition focuses on the history of the Mongol Empire and its central ruler, Genghis Khan. title: Hauser & Wirth debuts Cindy Sherman's new 'Fabric Matrons' series in London
summary: This fall, Cindy Sherman debuts photographic works from her new Fabric Matrons series, which explores identity as a continual process of construction over a lifetime. Shaped by a visual vocabulary of elaborately draped fabrics, the protagonists in Sherman's images appear to dissolve into their surroundings, heightening the tension between concealment and display to examine how women negotiate visibility across different phases of life. Sherman's staged scenes, several of which incorporate elements drawn from Chanel's archives, foreground the performance—and perception—of femininity and beauty, probing the societal expectations and enduring pressure to fashion and maintain a public image over time. Cindy Sherman found a starting point for this new series within the pages of a giveaway magazine from a high-end store in the Hamptons, filled with smooth, airbrushed images of a well-known model of Sherman's own generation, dripping in jewelry. title: Three Korean artists re-examine climate, crisis, and natural cycles in 'Aqua Paradiso'
summary: Aqua Paradiso was an exhibition curated in 2022 by the National Asian Culture Center (ACC). This contemporary art project brought together 11 artists from Asia and around the world to explore the theme of “water” from aesthetic, philosophical, and ecological perspectives. The exhibition took place over a three-month period at ACC in Gwangju, offering a multilayered examination of the primordial nature of life contained within water and its relationship with human society. Aqua Paradiso now continues in 2026 as a touring exhibition at Korean Cultural Centres in India and Australia. This edition features three of the Korean artists who took part in the original exhibition: Hyewon Kwon, Boo Jihyun, and Eunhae Jung (eco orot). Each uses a different visual language to approach the responsiveness and dynamics of water and the transformative sensibilities of the Anthropocene era. title: Metropolitan Museum of Art explores the secret design drawings of Tiffany Studios
summary: This fall, The Metropolitan Museum of Art presents Designing the Gilded Age: Drawings from the Studios of Louis C. Tiffany, a major exhibition exploring the creative process behind some of Tiffany Studios' most celebrated works. On view from October 22, 2026, through February 7, 2027, the exhibition brings together nearly 120 works from the Museum's collection—along with a select group of key loans—to examine the artistic range of Louis Comfort Tiffany and the collaborative studio that produced significant works of American decorative art. A major loan from the Chrysler Museum of Art reunites its monumental stained-glass window, Woman in a Pergola with Wisteria (1911), with the original wisteria transoms designed for the work. title: Andy Warhol's 'Cowboys and Indians' sets world auction record at Heritage
summary: Andy Warhol's vision of the American West reached new heights at Heritage Auctions on Oct. 22, when his complete Cowboys and Indians portfolio sold for $1,031,250, setting a world auction record for the suite. The result surpassed the previous record of $1,008,000, set at Sotheby's in 2022. This result also led Heritage's Prints & Multiples Signature® Auction to $3.85 million, the second-highest total for a Prints & Multiples auction in company history. The 150-lot sale drew 864 international bidders and achieved a 99% sell-through rate, with additional auction records for works by Frank Stella, Salvador Dalí and Rashid Johnson. "Breaking the world auction record for Cowboys and Indians is a tremendous achievement for our team and a thrilling result for our consignor," says Aviva Lehmann, Heritage's Deputy Chairman of Fine Art. title: Museo Casa de Cervantes presents Dora García: Dialogue of Dogs
summary: Dora García. Dialogue of Dogs: Cipión, Berganza, Freud, Joyce, Kafka, Mayakovsky, Gal Costa, Piglia, Lacan, Mallarmé, Bowie… resurrection is the second exhibition within the framework of the “House taken over” project, which is named after the story by the author Julio Cortázar. It is set up as an exhibition laboratory in which contemporary artists are invited to “take over” what was author Miguel de Cervantes’ house in Valladolid. The exhibition conceived by the artist Dora García, under the curatorship of Agustín Pérez Rubio, weaves a web of references that connect literature, psychoanalysis and popular culture through different times and spaces with a double guiding thread: metamorphosis and resurrection. title: OFFSCREEN Curatorial Prize 2026 awarded to Sarah Brahim and Andrea Geyer
summary: The OFFSCREEN Curatorial Prize is awarded annually to a noteworthy proposal in the exhibition. The prize is voted by the OFFSCREEN Curatorial Residents, leading thinkers around image-based practices from major institutions around the world who are invited to gather at OFFSCREEN each year. This year's residents came from Metropolitan Museum of Art (New York), M+ (Hong Kong), Museo Tamayo (Mexico), Museo Reina Sofia (Madrid), Smithsonian (Washington, DC), Singapore Art Museum and others. At OFFSCREEN's 5th Edition, at the Chapelle Saint-Louis de la Salpêtrière, the 2026 OFFSCREEN Curatorial Prize is awarded exceptionally to two proposals, by Sarah Brahim and by Andrea Geyer. title: Brognon Rollin awarded the 2026 Prix Marcel Duchamp
summary: On Thursday, October 22, 2026, the Prix Marcel Duchamp jury met to select the winner of the 2026 edition from this year's four nominees: Joël Andrianomearisoa, Brognon Rollin, Laura Henno and Josèfa Ntjam. The jury's deliberations followed presentations of the artists by their respective rapporteurs: Annabelle Ténèze for Joël Andrianomearisoa, Frère Marc Chauveau for Brognon Rollin, Isabelle Renard for Laura Henno and Cédric Fauq for Josèfa Ntjam. title: Russell Mills brings new immersive installation to Abbot Hall
summary: Inspired in part by the remarkable life of Kendal’s ‘Blind Philosopher’, John Gough, Darkness Visible, is a new installation by Russell Mills that invites visitors to slow down, listen closely and look again. Opening on 24 October at Abbot Hall, Kendal, the exhibition offers an experience that is never quite the same twice. Mills combines film, sound and generative technology to create a constantly changing landscape of images and sounds. Sequences collide and reform in unexpected ways, moving between moments of calm, curiosity and apprehension. There is no fixed beginning, middle or end; instead, visitors encounter an ever-shifting work shaped by chance and their own experience of it. For audiences in Cumbria, the work has a particularly strong local connection. Mills, who was born in Yorkshire in 1952, has been based in Ambleside

title: Maxim Gorki Theater presents Marco Fusinato IN THE CORPSE OF THE PRESENT
summary: Eight hours a day, for twenty-one days, across two floors of the Gorki Theater, artist and noise musician Marco Fusinato transforms Heinrich von Kleist’s Prinz Friedrich von Homburg into a durational performance-installation combining experimental sound, moving images, and live performance. Conceived specifically for the Gorki, IN THE CORPSE OF THE PRESENT marks Fusinato’s first work developed for the theatre. For more than two decades, his practice has moved between contemporary art and experimental music. He gained international recognition with DESASTRES, his 200-day performance-installation for the Australian Pavilion at the 2022 Venice Biennale. title: Uri Aran, Hao Jingban, and Will Stovall at MIT List Visual Arts Center
summary: The MIT List Visual Arts Center announced its fall 2026 exhibition and programming schedule. The galleries feature solo exhibitions by Uri Aran, Hao Jingban, and Will Stovall. Uri Aran’s first major institutional solo exhibition in the United States gathers new work made from materials typically found in the home or schoolroom: pompom fringe, keepsakes, craft supplies, sticker sheets, cartoon figures. Learning, and the effort and reward that sustain it, runs through his work. Classroom desks are heaped with googly eyes, sheets of animal stickers (a child’s micro-currency of approval) are enlarged to the scale of tapestries, and Duolingo’s characters brighten and slump on monitors that loom high above the viewer. title: Casino Luxembourg unveils 'The Hearth Room', an evolving experiment in artistic production
summary: Where does artistic work begin, and where does its production end? When does an exhibition start, and when does its preparation cease? The Hearth Room is not an exhibition where everything arrives finished; it evolves over time. What serves as a workspace today may transform into a stage tomorrow; what starts as raw material may end up as part of the installation’s architecture. For Christoph Meier and Ute Müller, their exhibition is not about displaying completed works; it is about revealing the context and conditions of production itself. title: Contemporary artist Rebecca Louise Law's latest floral sculpture now open at Newfields
summary: Rebecca Louise Law: Efflorescence transforms the Efroymson Family Entrance Pavilion into a breathtaking immersive environment. Suspended overhead in cascading layers, the large-scale installation is composed of approximately 37,000 dried flowers and plant elements harvested from across the Newfields campus and combined with over 1,000,000 flowers from the artists' collection. "Efflorescence perfectly represents the union between art and nature that Newfields is known for,” said Le Monte G. Booker Sr., President and CEO of Newfields. “Bringing this incredible work of contemporary art to the Efroymson Family Entrance Pavilion shows guests this union right when they walk through our doors and showcases the work of the local organizations and community members that helped bring this work to life.” Law is renowned for her monumental installations of preserved flowers and plants, transforming them into living archives that celebrate nature while reflecting on cycles of growth,

title: Sixty years after landmark Jewish Museum show, Bolzano exhibition re-examines Minimalism
summary: Sixty years after the landmark exhibition Primary Structures: Younger American and British Sculptors, held in 1966 at New York’s Jewish Museum, the Antonio Dalle Nogare Foundation is proud to present a new exhibition project that aims to celebrate and historically reconsider the legacy of Minimalism and its influence on contemporary art through a selection of works from the Collection. This new exhibition is curated by Eva Brioschi. Curated by Kynaston McShine, the 1966 exhibition established artists such as Donald Judd, Carl Andre, Dan Flavin, Robert Morris and Sol LeWitt, introducing a new concept of sculpture based on formal reduction, seriality and objectivity. title: Asia Society announces new, permanent home in Washington, D.C. for Policy Institute
summary: The Asia Society announced a new, permanent home in Washington, D.C. for its Policy Institute and Center for China Analysis at the Blaine Mansion at 2000 Massachusetts Avenue NW. The 15,000 square foot historic building in Dupont Circle—at the intersection of think tank and Embassy rows—will include offices, state-of-the-art conference facilities, convening spaces, and more. The Global President and CEO of the Asia Society, the Hon. Dr. Kevin Rudd AC said that “Asia Society’s purchase of the Blaine Mansion was made possible by a lead gift from Stephen A. Schwarzman, Chairman, CEO, and Co-Founder of Blackstone and Asia Society Global Trustee. title: The ICA at VCU presents Tony Cokes, Cassi Namoda, and Diane Severin Nguyen
summary: The Institute for Contemporary Art at Virginia Commonwealth University presents three solo exhibitions by multidisciplinary artists Tony Cokes, Cassi Namoda, and Diane Severin Nguyen, on view now through February 21, 2027, at the Markel Center. The fall exhibitions feature a survey spanning more than three decades of work by Richmond-born Cokes, new site-specific commissions by internationally recognized Namoda, and a kinetic sonic installation by Severin Nguyen. Together, the exhibitions explore film, photography, painting, sculpture, installation, and performance. Tony Cokes: Texts, Tracks, Talks (1992–2026) is a survey of Tony Cokes (b. 1956, Richmond, Virginia), whose politically charged video essays examine structural racism, power, visibility, and ideologies embedded in popular culture.
